title: ::before, ::after, ::marker, ::selection, ::placeholder
learningObjectives: Explain ::before, ::after, ::marker, ::selection, ::placeholder and use selectors or sizing rules appropriately.

understand.concept: Pseudo-elements style specific generated or specialised parts of elements. ::before and ::after create generated content boxes; ::marker styles list markers; ::selection styles selected text; ::placeholder styles placeholder text. Generated content should not carry essential information.
understand.whyItMatters: Generated content is not a replacement for meaningful HTML. Placeholder text is not a label, and decorative pseudo-elements should not be the only way to convey status or instructions.
understand.analogy: Pseudo-elements style parts of an element, like changing the appearance of a label's marker or selected text without adding a new HTML element.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies the idea; selector matching and sizing follow CSS specifications and browser layout algorithms.

explain.narrative: The label receives generated decorative text, list markers change colour, selected text uses a custom palette, and placeholder text is styled.

examples.explanation: The label receives generated decorative text, list markers change colour, selected text uses a custom palette, and placeholder text is styled.
examples.expectedOutput: A rendered example showing the selector or sizing behaviour described.

practise.guidedTask: Use ::marker and ::selection, then add decorative ::before content that does not repeat essential information. Keep a real label for the input.
practise.independentTask: Build a short example that demonstrates the topic with realistic content. Inspect matched selectors or computed sizes in developer tools.
hints: Check which elements match each selector.
Avoid relying on decorative generated content for meaning.
